articles.title: Open-Source AI Gets Leaner, Security Gets a Scorecard
articles.content: Developers just got a double dose of good news: a new open-source model proves that smaller can be smarter, while a dedicated leaderboard is finally bringing clarity to AI security. Thinking Machines debuted Inkling-Small, an open-source AI model that's roughly a quarter the size of its predecessor but delivers nearly identical performance. This isn't just about efficiency; it's a signal that accessible, high-performing models are becoming a standard, pushing the boundaries of what's possible with fewer resources. Simultaneously, a new AI Security Leaderboard has emerged, directly ranking the robustness and security of frontier models. This development addresses a critical gap, offering concrete benchmarks for developers and teams tasked with deploying AI safely and reliably. For anyone building with AI, these advancements mean more powerful, resource-efficient tools are becoming available, paired with clearer guidance on how to secure them against emerging threats.
bullets: AI Security Leaderboard: Ranks frontier model robustness.

articles.title: OpenAI Slashing Prices as AI Cost Wars Heat Up
articles.content: The gloves are off in the AI model market. OpenAI just delivered massive price cuts, signaling a new era where cost-efficiency isn't just a perk — it's a battleground. OpenAI dramatically cut prices for its GPT-5.6 Luna model by 80% and Terra by 20%. This aggressive move isn't happening in a vacuum; DeepSeek simultaneously launched its V4-Flash API, boasting a 60% lower cost per task than GPT-5.6 Luna, alongside a significant performance leap. These developments highlight a clear trend: the race to the bottom on AI inference costs is accelerating. For businesses, this means the barrier to entry for advanced AI capabilities is rapidly falling, but it also demands a sharper focus on evaluating models not just on raw power, but on their operational efficiency and total cost of ownership. Any company still treating AI as a luxury rather than a strategic commodity just had their wake-up call.

articles.title: LinkedIn Takes a Stand Against 'AI Slop'
articles.content: If your social media feed feels flooded with generic, AI-generated content, you're not alone. LinkedIn just gave users a direct weapon against the rising tide of "AI slop." LinkedIn rolled out a new feature allowing users to flag posts that "seem like AI slop," even replacing its own AI writing assistant with a simpler proofreading tool. This move is a direct response to the increasing volume of low-quality, unoriginal content flooding professional networks. It signifies a critical shift: platforms are now actively fighting to maintain content integrity and user trust in an era where AI can generate text at scale. For the average user, this means a potential cleaner feed and a clearer distinction between genuine human insight and automated noise.

articles.title: DeepMind's Gemini Robotics 2: AI's Leap into the Physical World
articles.content: Forget just talking to AI; Google DeepMind just unveiled an AI model capable of controlling entire humanoid robots with nuanced, whole-body motions. Google DeepMind's Gemini Robotics 2 represents a major stride in AI's ability to interact with the physical world. This new model can direct complex, full-body movements in humanoid robots, moving beyond isolated tasks to coordinated physical control. For students interested in AI, this breakthrough opens up entirely new avenues in robotics, human-robot interaction, and the practical application of advanced AI. It signals a future where AI isn't just processing data, but physically engaging with environments, offering a glimpse into the next generation of intelligent systems that will demand interdisciplinary skills.

articles.title: AI Agents Are Learning to Code in Your Browser, Opening New Creative Doors
articles.content: Forget clunky interfaces; AI agents are now gaining the ability to run code directly within your browser, a development that could reshape how artists interact with generative tools. The release of Datasette Agent 0.4a0 introduces a new mechanism allowing AI agent tools to execute code directly in the user's browser. This isn't just a technical tweak; it's a shift towards more interactive and integrated AI capabilities. For artists, this means the potential for generative AI tools to become far more responsive, customizable, and deeply integrated into existing digital workflows without constant back-and-forth with external servers. Imagine agents that can dynamically adjust parameters, generate variations, or even script complex animations directly within your creative environment, offering a new frontier for interactive and personalized artistic expression.
